items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: I used to sit in for a couple of numbers with his group.

ctx.x: I had not heard many jazz violinists because voilins were not played as a jazz instrument, although there were some orchestras that used violins in a very commercial way in some arrangements. I've heard the best jazz violinist since the first time I've heard Juice and to my estimation, there never was one greater than Robert "Juice" Wilson

Juice was playing clarinet also and I used to sit in for a couple of numbers with his group. But the violin was the instrument that he would cut everybody on, so he only brought his clarinet along to the saloon after he had finished his job. I suppose he was called "Juice" because of his drinking habit, but I never saw him drinking more than anyone else.

Cecil Scott stayed in the same place where I stayed which was not far from the jam session saloon and one morning he was so [loaded] leaded that I had to bring him home. That was not an easy job because I weighed 145 pounds and Cecil was on the short fattish side and weighed around 175 pounds. But I managed to get him home and in the bed and then I went back to the saloon. When I came home a few hours later, I looked in Cecil's room to see if he was alright, he had rolled out of bed and was snoring on the floor…
